name: arc-three-color-rays
description: Use when an ARC grid has three adjacent colored cells at an edge and matching isolated edge markers. Extend each color as perpendicular rays.
---

# ARC: three-color rays with side markers

## Trigger
A sparse ARC grid has three consecutive nonzero cells in a row near the top (or analogous strip), typically three distinct colors, plus isolated cells matching those colors on the left or right edges.

## Rule inferred from demonstrations
Treat the adjacent three-color strip as the starts of three parallel rays, one per color, extending vertically in their respective columns. For each color with a matching isolated marker at a side edge, draw a horizontal ray of that color from the edge marker to the corresponding vertical-ray column, inclusive. The vertical ray of that color terminates at the marker's row; do not continue it beyond the horizontal crossbar. A color with no matching side marker continues vertically to the opposite grid boundary. Original seed cells remain.

The colors' column positions are the three positions in the starting strip, in order. Matching markers can appear at either side; draw the crossbar toward that color's column. In the demonstrated tasks, two colors had side markers and one did not.

## Worked pattern
For a seed strip `[5,3,8]` at columns 4–6, a 5 marker at left edge row 4 makes row 4 columns 0–4 equal 5 and the 5 vertical ray ends there; an 8 marker at right edge row 5 makes row 5 columns 6–11 equal 8 and ends its vertical ray there; a 3 marker at left row 8 makes row 8 columns 0–5 equal 3 and ends its vertical ray there. The 3 column is drawn from the seed row down through row 8. The unmarked color extends to the grid boundary.

## Procedure
1. Identify the three adjacent seed colors and their columns.
2. Find matching isolated side-edge markers and associate each with its matching seed color/column.
3. Extend each seed color vertically from the seed row toward the opposite edge. Stop at its matching marker's row, inclusive; if no marker, continue to the boundary.
4. On each marker row, fill the horizontal segment between that side edge and the color's seed column, inclusive.
5. Preserve zeros and all original cells not overwritten by these lines. Check dimensions and ensure crossings/cells agree with the intended rays.

## Pitfall
Do not blindly extend all three vertical lines through the whole grid, and do not extend a marked color's vertical segment beyond its crossbar. Earlier wrong guesses came from allowing rays to continue below their marker rows or incorrectly assuming the seed strip itself should be repeated across unrelated rows.",

# Three-color rays with side markers

## Trigger
A sparse ARC grid has three consecutive nonzero cells in a row near the top, generally three distinct colors, plus isolated cells on the left or right edge matching one or more of the three colors.

## Rule
Each cell of the three-color strip starts a vertical ray in its column, continuing toward the opposite boundary. If a color has a matching isolated marker on either side edge, stop that color's vertical ray at the marker's row, inclusive, and fill a horizontal segment on that row from the marked edge to the color's seed column, inclusive. A seed color without a matching side marker continues vertically to the boundary. Preserve the original cells.

## Procedure
1. Identify the three seed colors and their columns.
2. Associate each edge marker with the matching seed color's column.
3. Draw that color vertically from its seed row through the marker row; if unmarked, continue to the grid boundary.
4. Fill the horizontal marker-row segment from the edge to the corresponding seed column.
5. Leave other cells unchanged and verify rows/columns carefully.

## Demonstration pattern
With seed colors `[5,3,8]` at columns 4–6, a left-edge 5 marker at row 4 causes vertical 5 through row 4 and a horizontal 5 segment to column 4. A right-edge 8 marker at row 5 causes vertical 8 through row 5 and fills the segment from its seed column through the right edge. A left-edge 3 marker at row 8 similarly stops vertical 3 and fills to its seed column. Unmarked colors extend to the boundary.

## Common error
